review_method: Viewed actual Blender PNGs: all32 close drawings in two ordered boards, matched V030/V031 key board, individual F13/F20/F26 close frames, and selected actual1280x720 shot frames. This is frame/sequence inspection, not observed continuous playback.
visible_findings: Fuller V030 torso/thigh/calf family remains legible across both steps. Original head, collar and boot pigmentation is retained.
Contact/down/passing/up families now have intervening drawings. Second load was revised after first proof showed too little pelvis settle.
First passing has a clear raised-foot projection; the opposite passing shows the near thigh/calf and cuff without the old ribbon-leg contour.
Outer chest/shoulder is rounded; the full-width dark waist belt was replaced with a partial oblique seam. Body contour compresses at down and opens toward up.
F13 foreground hand clears the hem. Around passing and opposite loading the hand intentionally crosses the coat face; it remains a rough occlusion rather than a presentation pose.
Stable profile preserves head/hair silhouette throughout; there is no attempted head turnaround.
remaining_visual_issues: Arm action is still restrained, with some near-hand/coat merging around F11-F12 and F25-F28; independent playback must judge whether the arc is sufficiently clear.
There is an asymmetry in loading height caused by the differently projected painted boots and deliberate body-height breakdowns. It may still read unevenly in motion.
The body shading is a clean, flat construction fill and remains visually different from the retained painted head/boots. This is not final ink-and-wash finish.
This is a boy-only walk construction study, not the completed two-child supported recovery scene, clasp, stumble or restart transition.
next_gate: Request independent normal-speed construction review through parent; do not promote technical checks into visual approval.
